tasks.short: Evaluate emerging marketing technologies and recommend limited trials or adoption.

steps.what: Research emerging options through the {OTHER} research browser.

loop.input: A fixed set of public documentation, research and supplier claims.
loop.output: Source-linked capability, limitation and evidence cards.
loop.check: Require source passages and dates. Separate supplier claims from measured results; a person checks material claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per source; unresolved claims remain marked unverified.
loop.why_not_simpler: Descriptions and limitations appear in varied prose that fixed fields cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Export campaign results from the {ADS}, {BI} and {CRM}.
Compare strategic fit, costs and evidence in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Run a limited trial through the {ADS} where feasible.
Write an adoption recommendation in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Reviewed evidence cards, shortlist rationale and available pilot results.
loop.output: A recommendation draft with uncertainties, costs and a proposed next decision.
loop.check: Recalculate figures deterministically; require references for factual claims and strategist approval before circulation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence becomes an explicit limitation.
loop.why_not_simpler: The explanation must connect varied evidence to the campaign's specific trade-offs.

steps.what: Discuss the recommendation and decide the next commitment.

tasks.design: A portable evidence-card template and import job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} join reviewed research to campaign baselines from the {ADS}, {BI} and {CRM}. Bounded loops extract evidence and draft the recommendation; configured trials enforce approved budgets, dates and stop limits in the {ADS}. The strategist judges fit, and the marketing manager authorises each external trial and subsequent commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research was fragmented, campaign measures were inconsistent, and evidence needed substantial manual synthesis. Strategic fit was never a simple scoring problem.
tasks.enabler_now: Code assistance lowers the effort of building imports, checks and templates. Bounded extraction can prepare source-linked evidence without pretending to resolve strategic uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Small trials may not establish incremental value. Platform restrictions, weak attribution and changing capabilities make comparisons expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a promising technology solves the wrong customer problem, and stop an attractive but uninformative trial.

ambition.what: Weekly continue, stop or investigate decisions for emerging-channel trials.

tasks.altitude: Less of the week goes to collecting evidence and formatting recommendations. With delegated trial limits, the strategist can stop weak tests sooner; new spending commitments still require the marketing manager.

reach.task: Allocate a limited experimental marketing budget.
reach.learn: Incrementality, opportunity cost and portfolio-level experiment design.

evidence.claim: Campaign imports, fixed evaluation templates and bounded research synthesis are feasible patterns; this digest provides no direct search-marketing implementation.
A documented report failure supports checking generated claims against actual sources; it does not establish the proposed workflow's accuracy.

assumptions: Time shares estimate active work, excluding waiting; trials are used when a meaningful small test is possible.
The initial kit can use public sources and authorised aggregate exports before company integrations exist.
Trial budgets, measurement windows and stop conditions can be specified before launch.
Build ranges cover one team's initial workflow, not a universal research service.
GDPR applies to campaign data and EU AI Act duties depend on intended use; this workflow is not assumed high-risk merely because it uses a model.
unknowns: Which campaign and outcome exports the customer can access.
Whether tracking consent and outcome definitions support valid comparisons.
Who can authorise trials and delegate stop decisions.
Whether the proposed data use triggers consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which repeatable trial designs distinguish incremental outcomes from attribution changes?
Which sources permit reliable, dated extraction of capability and pricing claims?
new_work: Review extracted claims and unresolved contradictions.
Maintain source dates, import mappings and evaluation criteria.
Investigate failed trial checks and enforce stop limits.
Remove stale evidence when capabilities or commercial terms change.

tasks.short: Build editorial relationships and agree relevant hyperlink placements.

steps.what: Inspect prospective publishers through the {OTHER} research browser.

loop.input: A fixed list of public pages, campaign criteria and approved content.
loop.output: Relevance suggestions with supporting page excerpts and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Validate page availability and duplicates deterministically; a person checks editorial fit and questionable publishers.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair pass per page; ambiguous prospects await human review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Topical relevance and editorial context depend on free text rather than domain metrics alone.

steps.what: Update contacts, owners and outreach status in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Draft a relevant placement proposal in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved content, verified publisher context and permitted outreach history.
loop.output: A concise placement proposal citing a specific editorial connection.
loop.check: Require supporting source text; reject invented familiarity, commitments and unsupported performance claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; insufficient context produces a blank rationale for the person.
loop.why_not_simpler: A useful proposal must explain a specific connection between two pieces of content.

steps.what: Send the placement proposal through the {EMAIL}.
Discuss editorial value and placement terms through the {EMAIL}.
Approve wording, destination and disclosure through the {EMAIL}.
Check published links with the {OTHER} site crawler.

tasks.design: A configured outreach register in the {CRM} replaces the tracking workbook and checks duplicates, contact restrictions and ownership. A bounded loop prepares source-linked relevance notes and proposal drafts; the strategist approves each send through the {EMAIL} and handles negotiation. A scheduled checker on the {DATA_PLATFORM} compares published links with the agreed brief and records exceptions in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact history, drafts and placement checks lived in separate places. Editorial trust and negotiated terms could not be reduced to a mail sequence.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured records and sending controls handle the administration. Small text loops can prepare specific proposals, while inexpensive code checks live links.
tasks.still_hard: Replies are unpredictable, editorial control belongs to the publisher, and placement quality cannot be inferred from link counts.
tasks.human_edge: Offer a useful editorial reason to collaborate, recognise reputational risk and negotiate without damaging the relationship.

ambition.what: Relevant small specialist publishers previously missed by broad outreach lists.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to logging contacts and checking links; more goes to substantive publisher conversations. With delegated editorial criteria, the strategist can decline unsuitable placements directly; commercial concessions retain existing approval limits.

reach.learn: Editorial independence, audience fit, disclosure and relationship stewardship.

evidence.claim: Contact registers, duplicate suppression, approved sending and link checks can use configuration and deterministic code.
Bounded drafting can reduce preparation effort, but the digest provides no direct evidence for successful hyperlink negotiation.

assumptions: The strategist seeks useful editorial placements rather than indiscriminate bulk outreach.
The publisher controls publication; external production and waiting time are outside these effort shares.
A personal starter kit can begin with an authorised contact file and proposal templates.
The customer establishes a GDPR lawful basis, retention limits and applicable national electronic-marketing rules before outreach.
No employee monitoring is introduced; if introduced, consultation under national rules needs separate scope.
unknowns: Whether contact records and outreach history may be reused for this purpose.
Which publishers require commercial approval or specific disclosure.
Whether a usable {CRM} and approved {EMAIL} connection already exist.
Which destinations and publication promises require brand approval.
research_questions: Which relevance signals predict a useful editorial conversation rather than merely a reply?
Which link and disclosure attributes can be checked reliably across publisher formats?
new_work: Review relevance suggestions and proposed recipients.
Maintain contact restrictions, ownership and retention settings.
Handle publisher replies and broken or changed placements.
Update link rules and investigate crawler failures.

tasks.short: Evaluate marketing technology, reuse existing capacity and procure approved tools.

steps.what: Define campaign requirements and acceptance criteria in the {DOCS}.
Check contracts and the {OTHER} IT asset register for reusable licences.
Compare supplier quotes and total costs in the {SPREADSHEET}.

loop.input: A fixed set of quotes, commercial terms and capability documents.
loop.output: Source-linked prices, units, limits, renewal terms and capability claims.
loop.check: Validate currency, billing period and mandatory fields; calculate totals with code and review uncertain terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unresolved terms block a complete comparison.
loop.why_not_simpler: Quotes express usage tiers, exclusions and renewal terms in inconsistent prose and tables.

steps.what: Test shortlisted tools in the {OTHER} evaluation environment.
Review security, data use and integration risks in the {DOCS}.
Agree the selected tool and approve the budget.
Enter the approved requisition in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Check policy and issue the purchase order through the {PROCUREMENT}.

tasks.design: A requirements form in the {WORKFLOW} checks available contracts and the {OTHER} IT asset register before starting a purchase. A bounded extractor builds a quote comparison, while deterministic code calculates costs; the strategist and IT reviewer test suitability and risk. Approved choices populate the {PROCUREMENT}, whose existing controls gate the external purchase order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Licence availability, commercial terms and purchasing records were disconnected. Tool suitability and data risks still required practical evaluation.
tasks.enabler_now: Code assistance makes small register adapters and comparison checks cheaper to build. Bounded extraction handles variable quote formats; existing purchasing controls handle approvals.
tasks.still_hard: Contract interpretation, real integration effort and supplier lock-in remain difficult. Low purchase frequency can make bespoke integrations uneconomic.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an impressive demonstration from a tool that fits the team's actual work, support capacity and risk tolerance.

ambition.what: Quarterly marketing licence reuse and retirement decisions.

tasks.altitude: Occasional purchases require less comparison paperwork, freeing time for hands-on evaluation and licence reviews. No purchasing authority changes unless explicitly delegated; budget and contract commitments retain their existing owners.

reach.task: Review the marketing technology portfolio for renewal or retirement.
reach.learn: Total ownership cost, adoption measures, switching cost and supplier exit planning.

evidence.claim: Quote extraction with deterministic cost calculation is a feasible pattern; the digest does not document marketing technology selection.
A vendor case documents reduced requisition review effort in procurement; it does not establish equivalent results for marketing purchases.

assumptions: Shares cover active evaluation and purchase coordination across the named roles, excluding supplier waiting time.
The starter kit uses approved quote files and register exports; live integration is worthwhile only if reused across purchases.
Trials use synthetic or approved data and do not publish campaigns or incur unapproved spending.
GDPR, EU AI Act obligations and national rules are assessed against the selected tool's actual intended use.
Access estimates include ordinary internal consultation; formal employee consultation or contract negotiation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether licence allocation and usage records are complete enough to establish reuse.
Which security, privacy, legal and budget approvals are mandatory.
Whether the selected tool changes employee monitoring and requires consultation under national rules.
Whether purchasing volume justifies live integration rather than file imports.
Which supplier quotes and contracts may be processed in the chosen environment.
research_questions: Which commercial fields drive most comparison errors across typical supplier quotes?
Can existing purchasing configuration accept an approved comparison without a custom requisition adapter?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous quote terms and maintain extraction checks.
Maintain licence mappings, cost assumptions and acceptance criteria.
Review failed policy checks and duplicate requisitions.
Reassess supplier data use, renewal terms and tool adoption.

tasks.short: Collaborate with designers and editors on search-ready content that follows the brand.

steps.what: Prepare the content and search brief in the {DOCS}.
Agree the concept and creative constraints with designers and editors.
Draft headings, page copy and metadata in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved claims, audience intent, page structure and brand examples.
loop.output: Draft headings, page copy and metadata with claim references.
loop.check: Check required fields, length and prohibited terms with code; a person reviews accuracy, tone and usefulness.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims are omitted and unresolved wording returns to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Original page language and tone require contextual writing beyond filling fixed template fields.

steps.what: Review search hierarchy and visual execution in the {OTHER} design editor.
Relay consolidated revision notes through the {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
Approve the staged page and resolve brand exceptions in the {CMS}.
Publish the approved page through the {CMS}.

tasks.design: A configured brief template in the {DOCS} assembles approved fields, while a bounded loop prepares copy drafts from approved claims. Designers and the strategist record feedback together in the {PROJECT}, removing the separate relay of revision notes; deterministic staging checks flag missing fields, invalid links and accessibility issues. The {CMS} publishes only the exact revision covered by the brand manager's approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Creative decisions crossed disciplines, and feedback was duplicated across documents and messages. Brand guidance included examples and exceptions that could not be fully encoded.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates, shared annotations and publication controls already address much of the coordination. Code assistance lowers the cost of checks, and bounded drafting shortens copy preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Visual originality, accessible multimedia and competing stakeholder preferences need skilled collaboration. Automated checks do not establish that a page communicates well.
tasks.human_edge: Reconcile search intent, brand expression and visual hierarchy without sacrificing clarity or creative quality.

ambition.what: An early search-and-content review clinic for campaign designers.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time rebuilding briefs and forwarding comments, and joins creative work earlier. With delegation, they can accept routine search changes within agreed guidelines; brand exceptions and publication approval remain with the brand manager.

reach.task: Review page hierarchy against audience intent.
reach.learn: Semantic structure, accessible interaction, responsive layouts and visual hierarchy.

reach.task: Assess page copy for clarity and supported claims.
reach.learn: Editorial standards, claim substantiation and consistent voice.

evidence.claim: Shopify Sidekick supports product-description drafting; this is narrow evidence for copy assistance, not for complete multimedia design.
Brief templates, shared feedback and revision-specific publication controls can be configured or built deterministically.

assumptions: The brief uses structured, approved fields; it does not require automatic synthesis of new research.
Design concepts and staged pages arrive from the collaborating production team; their full production effort is outside these shares.
The starter kit consists of portable brief fields, copy checks and review criteria before live connections are added.
Publication approval is collected in s6 and enforced in s7 without requesting a second approval.
GDPR applies where personal data appears in content or assets; EU AI Act transparency duties depend on the actual content and use.
No employee monitoring is introduced; consultation under national rules is scoped separately if that changes.
unknowns: Whether brand guidance and approved claims are current and accessible.
Whether collaborators can share one review location.
Whether the {CMS} can bind approval to a specific revision and invalidate it after changes.
Which asset rights, accessibility requirements and publication approvals apply.
research_questions: Which repeated review comments can become useful deterministic staging checks?
Which brief fields prevent the most late creative rework?
new_work: Review generated copy and verify supporting claims.
Maintain templates, brand examples and staging checks.
Resolve conflicting annotations and accessibility exceptions.
Maintain revision-specific approval and publication controls.

role.altitude: The week shifts from gathering evidence, copying records and relaying comments toward experiments, editorial relationships and creative trade-offs. Any added rights should be explicit: stopping bounded trials, declining unsuitable placements and accepting routine search changes within agreed limits.
reach: Marketing manager: contribute evidence to experiment funding and technology renewal decisions.
Public relations specialist: develop useful editorial partnerships.
Web and digital interface designer: shape page hierarchy around audience intent.
Editor: improve clarity and substantiate content claims.
skills_to_grow: Technology ownership costs and supplier evaluation.
Accessible content structure and visual review.
Maintaining small integrations, checks and bounded drafting workflows.
role.ambitious_version: Run a regular search opportunity review that connects emerging-channel trials, editorial partnerships and content improvements to measured customer outcomes, with clear budget and publication limits.
